title: Maj. Silas Harlan

bodyMarkdown:
Virginia-born Major Silas Harlan (c. 1752–1782) came to Kentucky in 1774, built Harlan's Station on the Salt River about seven miles south of Harrodsburg in 1778, and commanded spies in George Rogers Clark's Illinois campaign. Clark later said he was "one of bravest soldiers that ever fought by my side." Harlan fell leading an advance party at Blue Licks on August 19, 1782, and was buried on the field; Harlan County, created in 1819, is named for him.
Source: [County Named, 1819 — Kentucky Historical Marker 785 (Kentucky Historical Society)](https://history.ky.gov/markers/county-named-1819)
